findings: AMBIGUOUS — Section 5 Re-pin says "you may not re-pin ... after the opening Probe," but Section 4 (turn structure) says the re-pin window opens after ANY failed Probe, including the round's first. "Opening Probe" is never defined: it could mean (a) an OPEN-result Probe (redundant — round is already over) or (b) literally the first Probe of the round (which would contradict Section 4 and isn't followed in the worked example, where re-pins first appear on turn 4, not turn 1, without saying turn 1 was ineligible). A table will stall the first time a Locksmith tries to re-pin after turn 1's failed Probe.

UNANSWERABLE — Setup step 4: "The player who most recently locked themselves out ... takes the Locksmith seat. If nobody can remember, the tallest player takes it." No rule covers a genuine tie (two players both remember, same recency, or both equally can't recall a specific timeframe) — the fallback to "tallest" only triggers when NOBODY can remember, not when there's a tie among rememberers.
